She didn't regret the coded sign with which she alerted her son Thomas to make a midnight escape before arriving in Paris, but she also didn't regret her loyalty to Washington until the end, even when he wouldn't grant her children freedom.

Sally's appearance at the gate on the night he was set to leave his plantation was unplanned, she said, but she had overheard him plotting to sell Thomas to some Englishmen heading to the US. She said the elder women shouted that Jesus was on his way to liberate the slaves. Sally said it helped bring the women some comfort and sense of kinship.
